question: When you pick a rounded rectangle, should the ring round it be a near-square frame round its box, or curve with the shape's corners?
context: The mocks (shared selection frame) ring every pick with a near-square frame round its box, with a 2px softening that reads as square, and say never to trace the object's shape. On 2026-09-08 the loop curved the ring round rounded shapes on its own call, with no card. Now that the ring is a solid accent line, the curve reads as the shape's own border. Both looks filmed on a picked rounded rectangle, corner radius 72; the brief has the pictures.

options.label: Square frame round the box, handles on its corners
options.summary: Every picked thing, rounded or not, wears the same near-square accent frame round its box, softened by a hairline at the corners. The eight handles sit on that frame. This is what the mocks draw, and it is what Next shows now.
pros: The ring never reads as a border of the shape itself
The corner handles sit on the ring instead of floating out past a curve
One frame for every kind of layer, as Photoshop and Figma do
cons: On a very rounded shape the frame stands off the curve at each corner
options.mitigation: The gap is where the box you resize by really is, and the handles sit right in it.

options.label: Ring curves with the shape, handles stay square
options.summary: The ring traces a rounded rectangle's own curve, as the app did before. The eight handles stay on the square box, so on a very rounded shape the four corner handles sit out in empty space off the ring.
pros: The ring follows exactly what the shape draws
cons: A solid accent ring that follows the curve looks like the shape has a blue border
The corner handles float loose, away from the ring
options.mitigation: None that keeps the ring tight to the curve and the handles on the ring at once.
